- **Authority and source:** Proposed resolution, Bill No. R-26-09-17 as amended, titled as a temporary moratorium on certain data-center approvals; its separate resolution-number line is blank. October 13, 2026 regular-session minutes, entry IV, record failure 4-4. The minutes’ generic Ordinance Number label does not establish an adopted ordinance. Entry III records the separate CIERC proposal, G-26-09-16 as amended as amended, failing 3-5.
- **What prompted it:** The proposal’s recitals sought time to review data-center definitions, development standards and impacts on electrical capacity, water and wastewater systems, public infrastructure, land and community resources while the zoning code lacked comprehensive standards for large-scale data-center development.
- **Affected projects:** The rejected proposal concerned final discretionary Common Council approvals for new hyperscale or large-scale data-center developments, aggregating related phases, expansions and facilities under common ownership/control, contiguous sites, shared infrastructure or the same planned development. It excluded principally telecommunications and emergency-communications facilities and preserved prior lawfully granted approvals. It requested corresponding measures by other approving bodies without directing action beyond their legal authority, and allowed study/planning/review short of final Council approval. The failed bill imposed no moratorium on any project.
- **Status notes:** Rejected: the October 13, 2026 regular-session minutes record amended Bill R-26-09-17 failing 4-4. Ayes: Booker, Ensley, Jehl and Paddock; nays: Bender, Chambers, Hartman and Myers. Thomas Freistroffer was absent. The mayor-signature field is N/A. This records the disposition of that proposal; a distinct later proposal requires its own identity review.
- **Outcome:** Amended Bill R-26-09-17 failed 4-4 on October 13, 2026; no moratorium was enacted by that bill. The separate CIERC proposal failed 3-5 and is not the moratorium vote.

- **Status:** Last recorded action: first reading and referral to Senate Utilities 2026-01-08; session ended 2026-02-27. An advocacy tracker reported the bill died without a hearing; committee records were not independently reviewed.
- **Provisions:** Failed introduced proposal: large-load class covers one customer or up to four customers requesting aggregate new/additional demand exceeding the lesser of 5% of the utility’s three-year average peak demand or 150 MW. Standard tariffs offered after March 14, 2026 would require reimbursement of all reasonably allocable project costs even if anticipated service is not taken. The LSA introduced fiscal note describes this as replacing an at-least-80% reimbursement requirement; this is proposed change analysis, not proof of current law. Other provisions would cap certain basic-rate increases, restrict recovery of specified political/other expenses, and urge a 2026 interim tracker study. The generic load class and fiscal note do not independently establish a qualifying data-center application.
- **Mechanism / scope:** utility_large_load_restriction; utility_grid
- **Legal effect:** failed
- **Effective date:** —
- **End condition and limitations:** Introduced section 5 would expire 2027-01-01; this is the proposed tracker-study provision, not a whole-bill sunset.
- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://iga.in.gov/pdf-documents/124/2026/senate/bills/SB0234/SB0234.01.INTR.pdf>)

### SB 257

- **Policy ID:** `in-sb-257`
- **Sponsor / party:** Sen. Chris Garten; R
- **Status:** Last recorded action: first reading and referral to Senate Utilities 2026-01-08; session ended 2026-02-27. An advocacy tracker reported no hearing; committee records were not independently reviewed.
- **Provisions:** Introduced proposal would bar IURC approval of an electric utility rate increase to the extent related solely to service costs for a data center or an existing or proposed Indiana facility whose aggregate demand exceeds the lesser of 5% of the energy utility average peak demand over the most recent three calendar years or 150 MW and which has fewer than 50 full-time on-premises employees.
- **Mechanism / scope:** utility_large_load_restriction; utility_grid
- **Legal effect:** failed
- **Effective date:** —
- **End condition and limitations:** —
- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://iga.in.gov/pdf-documents/124/2026/senate/bills/SB0257/SB0257.01.INTR.pdf>)

### SB 79

- **Policy ID:** `in-sb-79`
- **Sponsor / party:** Sen. J.D. Ford; second author Sen. Spencer Deery; D; R
- **Status:** Last recorded action: Senator Deery added as second author 2026-01-06; session ended 2026-02-27. An advocacy tracker reported no hearing; committee records were not independently reviewed.
- **Provisions:** Introduced proposal would create an IURC working group on future data center electricity demand, require quarterly operator electricity-use reporting by source, and require local authorities to obtain projected full-capacity power and water use and perform a site assessment before issuing a construction permit.
